definitions.gloss: huge pile; heaping stack; mountain of things
definitions.explanation: A large quantity of items piled high, either literally (physical objects stacked up) or figuratively (an overwhelming number of tasks, problems, or issues).

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}が{山積|やまづ}みになっている。
examples.english: Documents are piled up in a mountain.

examples.japanese: {倉庫|そうこ}には{段|だん}ボールが{山積|やまづ}みにされていた。
examples.english: Cardboard boxes were stacked high in the warehouse.

examples.japanese: {解決|かいけつ}すべき{問題|もんだい}が{山積|やまづ}みで、{何|なに}から{手|て}をつけていいかわからない。
examples.english: There's a mountain of problems to solve, and I don't know where to start.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the pattern {山積|やまづ}みになっている (to be piled up) or {山積|やまづ}みにする (to pile up). Also used figuratively for abstract things like {課題|かだい} (issues) and {問題|もんだい} (problems).

RELATED:
The verb form {山積|さんせき}する is a more formal synonym used primarily in written or business contexts to describe accumulated problems: {問題|もんだい}が{山積|さんせき}している.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {山積|やまづ}みになる (to become piled up)
- {山積|やまづ}みにする (to pile up)
- {書類|しょるい}が{山積|やまづ}み (documents piled high)
- {問題|もんだい}が{山積|やまづ}み (a mountain of problems)
